evidence.note: Built /tmp/test_mapping.py to dump JAX pokedex parameter keys/shapes and compare against PyTorch state_dict — self-built check beyond benchmark's PASS/FAIL to verify weight mapping.

Created a series of parity/debug harnesses (test_parity.py, test_load.py, fix_attention.py, debug_parity.py) targeting weight loading, attention einsum, and output parity — repeated but ad hoc /tmp scripts rather than one reusable harness.

Explicit intermediate-tensor / per-layer localization: compares JAX vs PyTorch intermediate outputs, finds 'prefix tokens match well (max diff 0.0003)' to isolate the mismatch downstream — the hallmark of the level-8 anchor's per-layer discrepancy localization.
Uses benchmark's numerical comparison (max_abs ~2.9-4.0) as the end-to-end loss parity signal and iterates against it; treats it as evidence but supplements with own diagnostics.
Trajectory ends still debugging correctness; never reached optimization, so no optimized-vs-baseline output-equality gate was ever constructed — a required component of the level-8 anchor is absent.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: beyond running benchmark.py it built its own JAX-vs-PyTorch comparisons including intermediate/per-layer tensor localization (step 87 pinpointing that prefix tokens match at 0.0003), which the level-5 anchor explicitly lacks. It falls short of level 8 because the verification harnesses were ad hoc throwaway scripts rather than a clean reusable suite, the sampling path was checked only via the benchmark, and — because it never reached optimization — no optimized-vs-baseline output-equality gate was ever run. That places its observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.
